protocol.source_text:
CLINICAL FEATURES 
TRIAD – rigidity, muscle spasms & autonomic dysfunction 
* Contaminated wound may be trivial 
* Incubation period – 3-14 days ➔ time to first symptom 
* Onset time – 1-7 days ➔ time from first symptom to first spasm 
* Rigidity (persists > 2 weeks) 
-trismus, dysphagia, increased tone in trunk muscles 
* Spasms (reduce after 2 weeks) 
-laryngospasm, risus sardonicus, opisthotonos 
-may be spontaneous or provoked by physical/emotional 
stimuli 
* Autonomic disturbances (onset after spasms – lasts 1-2 weeks) 
-tachycardia & hypertension may alternate with 
bradycardia & hypotension, dysrhythmia, cardiac arrest 
-salivation, bronchial secretions 
-gastric stasis, ileus, diarrhoea 
* Respiratory compromise 
-chest wall rigidity 
-laryngospasm 
-aspiration 
 
COMPLICATIONS 
*Respiratory – aspiration, laryngospasm, apnoea, respiratory failure, ARDS, VAP 
*Cardiovascular – tachy/bradycardia, hyper/hypotension, ischaemia, cardiac failure 
*Renal – high output/oliguric renal failure, urinary stasis & infection 
*GIT – gastric stasis, ileus, diarrhoea, UGIB/LGIB 
*Musculoskeletal – rhabdomyolysis, fractures/tendon avulsions 2° spasms 
*Other – dehydration, thromboembolism, sepsis, MOD 
 
 
CAUSE 
*Clostridium tetani 
anaerobic spore forming gram positive bacillus 
*When spores germinate, and bacteria multiply ➔ 
toxins released i.e. tetanospasmin and tetanolysin 
TYPES 
*Cephalic / Local / Generalised / Neonatal 
 
DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS 
*Trismus 2 orofacial infection 
*Acute dystonic reactions 
*Hypocalcaemic tetany 
*Seizure disorder 
*Meningism 
*Psychogenic 
*Strychnine poisoning 
ED INVESTIGATIONS 
*U&E; CMP; CK; FBC 
*Blood cultures 
*ABG (respiratory failure) 
*U-dipstix 
*ECG
